title: Retrieval-augmented generation — Challenges
text:
Title: Retrieval-augmented generation — Challenges

RAG does not prevent hallucinations in LLMs. According to Ars Technica, "It is not a direct solution 
because the LLM can still hallucinate around the source material in its response." While RAG improves 
the accuracy of large language models (LLMs), it does not eliminate all challenges. One limitation is that while RAG 
reduces the need for frequent model retraining, it does not remove it entirely. Additionally, LLMs may struggle to 
recognize when they lack sufficient information to provide a reliable response. Without specific training, models may 
generate answers even when they should indicate uncertainty. According to IBM, this issue can arise when the model 
lacks the ability to assess its own knowledge limitations.
